albums.blurb: Paco de Lucía (1947–2014), from Algeciras in Andalusia, is the central figure of modern flamenco guitar, and this all-instrumental 1973 record is the pivot of his early discography. He cut it with his brother Ramón de Algeciras on second guitar plus bass and bongos — an unorthodox rhythm section for flamenco at the time — and the rumba "Entre dos aguas," improvised in the studio when the producer asked for a few more minutes of music, became the piece that carried flamenco guitar onto Spanish pop radio. The album set up his later Camarón de la Isla partnership and his jazz crossings with Al Di Meola and John McLaughlin.
albums.reception: "Entre dos aguas" rose up Spain's radio charts as a hit single — prompting the label to reissue the album in 1975 — and Fuente y Caudal is generally acknowledged to have marked a before-and-after for flamenco guitar.

albums.blurb: Before the studio experimentation of Sound & Color, the Athens, Alabama quartet's debut on ATO Records was raw Muscle Shoals-style soul-rock, recorded cheaply and led by Brittany Howard's volcanic voice on "Hold On" and "I Ain't the Same." It is the band's garage-soul origin story: bar-band economy, vintage tones, and songwriting that pulls equally from Otis Redding and southern rock. The band went on extended hiatus after 2018, with Howard moving to solo work.
albums.reception: Boys & Girls peaked at No. 6 on the Billboard 200, was later certified platinum, and earned the band three 2013 Grammy nominations including Best New Artist, while Rolling Stone voted "Hold On" the best song of 2012.

albums.blurb: Arooj Aftab is a Brooklyn-based, Lahore-raised composer and vocalist who studied at Berklee; Vulture Prince, her third album, released on New Amsterdam Records and dedicated to her late younger brother Maher, sets Urdu ghazal poetry over a chamber palette of harp, classical guitar, and upright bass rather than traditional South Asian instrumentation. It is the record that moved her from new-music circles to international audiences, and it led directly to Love in Exile, her 2023 trio album with Vijay Iyer and Shahzad Ismaily.
albums.reception: Its single "Mohabbat" won Best Global Music Performance at the 2022 Grammys — making Aftab the first Pakistani woman to win a Grammy — and gained a breakout moment when Barack Obama put it on his 2021 summer playlist.
